rationale.conceptual: The task requires implementing a standard but non-trivial method (molecular dynamics with Tersoff potential) and performing physics-based analyses (MSD, defect identification, efficiency calculation, cluster analysis). There is no novel algorithm, but careful translation of the published method into code is needed, and understanding of cascade physics is important.
rationale.execution: The pipeline involves many stages: setting up LAMMPS configurations for multiple energies, running a large number of cascade simulations (up to 15 low-energy and 5 high-energy) with system sizes up to 2 million atoms, performing trajectory analysis, and computing multiple quantitative outputs. The orchestration of simulation runs, data extraction, and formatting is complex and fragile.

difficulty.reasoning: The underlying work involves molecular dynamics with an established potential and well-defined analysis of cascade lifetime, defect production efficiency, and clustering. The method is non-trivial but well-documented, requiring careful implementation of MD simulations and post-processing. The pipeline is multi-stage, involving many simulation runs across energies and system sizes, which adds orchestration complexity.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Original work used a Cray T3E (CPU cluster) for the 30 keV cascade with 2 million atoms; a modern multi-core CPU with sufficient memory (~32 GB) can handle the largest simulation cell. No external dataset; only lattice generation and potential parameters are needed.
